title: Result Type Intro
story: Your calculator app needs to handle division — but dividing by zero crashes everything! Instead of crashing, you need a way to say 'this worked' OR 'this failed, here's why.'
why: The Result pattern is one of the most important enum patterns — it lets functions succeed with a value OR fail with an error message, all in one return type.
analogy: Result is like ordering at a restaurant. Either you get your food (Success with the meal) or you get an apology (Failure with the reason — 'we're out of that dish'). You never get nothing with no explanation.
try_it: Write a `validate_password` function that returns `MyResult.Success(length)` if the password is 8+ characters, or `MyResult.Failure("Too short!")` otherwise. Use `string.str_len()` to check.
tips: Return `Failure` immediately when something is wrong — don't compute the success case first
Every match on a Result must handle both Success and Failure — the compiler enforces this
Name payload fields clearly: `Success(value)` and `Failure(reason)` are the idiomatic names
common_mistakes: Returning `Failure` but forgetting to wrap it: `return "Error"` instead of `return MyResult.Failure("Error")`
Matching only `Success` and ignoring `Failure` — the compiler will catch this, but it's the most common surprise
Using different field names: `Success(result)` then matching with `Success(value)` — the pattern name must match the definition
